title: Keep the backlog sweep's vitest timeout clear of its CI wall time so a green tree stops timing out

source.ref: #4481 test job 2026-11-02: sweep case passed at 88,829ms against a 90,000ms timeout; #4482 re-run timed out at 90s on the same tree

detail:
The real-tree sweep case in backlog-contract.test.ts carried a 90s vitest timeout set when one full run took 20s. The list has since grown to 2,158 probes, and on 2026-11-02 the sweep read 88.8s of wall on CI (#4481, green by 1.2s) and timed out on the next PR (#4482) with nothing in that PR touching a probe's cost. The file's own doctrine (LIVE-047, ADR-1107) says wall time under contention is not a property of any probe and the budget is CPU: guardCpuMs against BASE + allowance x n, which read 314s against its budget and passed. So the wall clock had quietly become the gate. Fix: the sweep case's timeout goes to 360s and the per-PR case's to 180s (it read 50 to 53s against 90s), both documented as hang detectors, with the CPU assertions untouched. The probe reads both timeouts and fails when either is under 2x the wall measured that day.

 Fixed 2026-11-02.
